questions.prompt: "Even wealthy people face scarcity." Which statement best supports this claim?

choices.text: Wealthy people also have to pay taxes on their income.
Wealthy people also have limited time and must choose what to do.
Wealthy people often pay higher prices for the same goods.
The government decides how scarce each good should be.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the economic system found in most countries today?

choices.text: A traditional economy, where custom and past practice guide production and distribution
A command economy, where a government plan sets what is produced and in what amounts
A market economy, where trade alone decides, with no government rules or services
A mixed economy, where markets lead and government adds rules and public services

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a limitation or cost of specialization and the division of labor?

choices.text: The same resources tend to produce a smaller amount of output.
Workers have less need to trade what they produce with others.
Reliance on certain steps or regions can disrupt output if trade stops.
Workers tend to lose skill as they repeat the same familiar task.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Over the weekend, you volunteered for 4 hours instead of working a part-time job that pays $11 per hour (the job is worth more to you than resting). How much income, in dollars, did you give up by volunteering? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: With a $30 entertainment budget, you plan to spend the whole budget on theater tickets ($12 each) and tacos ($3 each). What is the opportunity cost of one theater ticket, measured in tacos? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: A school has already spent $50,000 on renovating its gym. Finishing the work would cost another $30,000, and the expected benefit of completing it is $20,000 (the $50,000 already spent cannot be recovered, and the $30,000 could instead pay for other school needs). Which judgment is most rational?

choices.text: Stop the work, since the future $30,000 cost exceeds the future $20,000 benefit.
Finish the work, since $50,000 is already spent and finishing would limit the loss.
Keep going, since the $20,000 benefit of finishing is still greater than zero.
Add the $50,000 already spent to the benefit and compare $70,000 with $30,000.

questions.prompt: Why does the production possibilities frontier bow outward?

choices.text: Resources suit different uses, so producing more of one good costs more and more of the other.
Technology improves each year, so the economy can produce more of both goods over time.
The two goods sell at the same price, so trading one for the other gets more costly.
Society prefers one of the goods, so it devotes a larger share of resources to it.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: For one unit of a product, the private cost is 40 cents and the social cost is $1.00 (100 cents). Buyers already pay a price equal to the private cost. What additional fee per unit, in cents, would make the price buyers pay equal to the social cost? (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: A school starts posting a weekly chart that shows how much food each class leaves uneaten. Which statement best describes this policy tool?

choices.text: It works through prices, raising the cost each student pays for wasted food.
It works through information and norms, making each class's waste visible to all.
It works through rules, limiting how much food can be served to each student.
It works through rewards, paying classes that cut their waste below a target.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes sustainable consumption?

choices.text: Buying as few goods as possible, whatever they are
Choosing the lowest-priced option for most purchases
Meeting needs with fewer resources and less waste
Buying large amounts of goods labeled as eco-friendly
